title: Opal Systems - Support Onboarding Scratchpad
body:
Context: quick working notes from discovery + first technical sync with Opal Systems (customer). They're a mid-market SaaS provider for customer support automation. This doc is my scratchpad for requirements, rough sequencing, and a friction/gotcha list to hand off to SE + infra later.

Meeting recap (2026-01-14):
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood), Samir (Redwood), Riley (Redwood), Priya Nair (Opal, Head of Platform), Tomas Eriksson (Opal, Lead Infra), Leah Park (Opal, Support CTO)
- Meeting length: 55m. High-level ask: replace current internal LLM endpoint (self-hosted on TF GPUs) with a solution that reduces 95th pct latency by 40% and halves per-100k-token cost for their chat summarization pipeline. Also need strong audit logs and on-prem option for one EU customer.

Business goals / success metrics:
- 95th pct token-generation latency target: <= 450ms for typical 128-token replies (today ~750ms)
- Cost target: <= $40 per 100k tokens equivalent across production traffic (today ~$95)
- Availability: 99.95% monthly for production support endpoints
- Data residency: EU-only for one named customer; rest of traffic US/EU multi-region acceptable
- Security: must support customer KMS + ability to bring customer-managed HSM for private deployment
- Observability: need per-request tracing that ties back to support ticket IDs; retention for 90 days

Primary technical constraints and notes:
- Current model: fine-tuned mix of Llama2-13B-instruct (quantized), served with a homegrown batching layer. They maintain a large cache of templated prompts and prefix context (50–150 tokens typical).
- Traffic profile: bursty during business hours (08:00–20:00 CET), steady tail overnight. Peak qps ~65 for inference requests, median 12. Important: multiple concurrent small requests (1–3 messages), so batching must not inflate tail latency.
- Integration points: support system (named "Helix") calls the LLM via an internal gRPC gateway. They want to preserve gRPC but are open to a lightweight adapter.
- PCI/PHI: No PHI, limited PCI scope (tokenization only). Still need strict access controls and audit logs.
- Model artifacts: they want to host their tuned model artifacts in S3-equivalent (compatible object storage) for private deployment. Need manifest for quantization and KV cache warm start.

Performance/engineering considerations (quick ideas):
- Dedicated instances with continuous batching tuned for short sequences; prefer batching window based on latency SLOs (e.g., 10–15ms max hold)
- Prefix/KV caching: leverage Redwood’s prefix caching to keep repeated templated prompts cached (Opal has high repetition across tickets)
- Mixed model routing: use cost-tier routing, route low-latency requests to smaller optimized variants for quick responses and fall back to larger model for long-form summarization
- Quantization guidance: Opal’s finetuned 13B model currently quantized to int4; need to validate accuracy regression with Redwood Optimize (run eval suite) before recommending a change

Security & compliance items:
- KMS integration: Opal requires the platform to support AWS KMS + ability to point to customer-managed key; ask SRE for HSM support checklist
- Audit logs: must include full request/response hashes and ticket id mapping. Retention 90 days; need to confirm retention cost and storage encryption at rest
- Private deployment: Opal asked for a VPC-hosted private control plane with option for on-prem inference nodes behind a firewall. Note: on-prem install will require an offline install bundle and install runbook.

Gotchas & red flags to confirm:
- Token accounting differences: their current infra counts tokens differently for multi-part messages; need to align on tokenization (tiktoken vs custom tokenizer). Risk: billing mismatch if not reconciled.
- Cold-starts for cached KV: their prefix diversity for some workflows is high (templates vary per customer), so prefix cache hit rate may be lower than they expect — need sample traffic to estimate cache effectiveness
- gRPC gateway compatibility: Helix's gateway expects streaming server-side semantics; need to validate Redwood adapter supports identical streaming behaviour and backpressure semantics
- Per-request tracing: currently no request-id propagation from Helix; integration effort to add the id into calls might be non-trivial across multiple services

Data/ops artifacts to request from customer (action items):
- Example traffic samples (anonymized) for 7 days covering business hours + weekend. Prefer NDJSON with request/response and ticketId fields.
- A copy of their fine-tune recipe and tokenizer specs (or pointer to S3 manifest)
- Current latency/cost telemetry per endpoint (95th/99th percentiles) and avg token lengths
- Network egress limits and IP allowlist for private deployment planning

Immediate next steps (owner tags):
- Maya: run quick cost/latency pre-check using sample perf profile (due 2026-01-20) — JIRA ticket JIRA-OPS-1298
- Samir: prototype a small Redwood adapter for Helix gRPC streaming to validate backpressure footprint (PoC demo by 2026-01-28)
- Riley: prepare KMS/HSM integration checklist and retention cost estimate for 90-day logs (due 2026-01-22)
- Opal (Priya/Tomas): send anonymized NDJSON traffic dump + tokenizer manifest (requested in thread)

Follow-ups planned:
- Deep-dive workshop (2h) week of 2026-01-25 to go through sample traffic and run Redwood Optimize evals. Invite list: Maya, Samir, Riley, Priya, Tomas, Leah, two Opal SREs.
- Internal sync with infra/SRE to review private-deploy runbook (Maya to schedule)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the PoC narrow: just gRPC adapter + small inference pool; demo latency improvement on 7-day sample window using Redwood’s batching and prefix cache.
- Watch out for billing mismatch: include a tokenization sanity check step in PoC so we can present an apples-to-apples cost comparison.
- If cache hit rate < 30% for certain ticket types, prepare fallback recommendation to use smaller model with aggressive quantization to hit latency target.

Attachments to prepare for next call:
- One-pager: expected perf delta and cost delta for three deployment options (hosted, dedicated, private) — include assumptions table
- Short checklist for Opal infra team to collect network/keys/logging info
- Demo plan: steps, acceptance criteria (latency target + no regression in top-5 prompt evals)

Unresolved questions (to ask on workshop):
- Which datastore stores ticket state and how easy is it to pipe ticketId into inference call?
- Confirm whether any customer data ever leaves EU for the named EU customer; need exact legal phrasing for contracts
- Do they have a feature-flagging service we can use for gradual rollout/canary?

End of scratchpad. Will convert to SE handoff doc once we have traffic sample and PoC results.
